title: Introduce scoped model-list filters, OpenAI preview flag, and pricing hint fields
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: product teams want richer discovery from the model catalog without having to pull the entire model index into client-side logic. This PR extends the public model-listing API with: 1) scoped filter profiles that encode common filter sets (latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, structured-output-first), 2) an opt-in OpenAI-compat preview flag on model entries so clients can discover which models currently support the OpenAI-style function-calling/structured-output shim, and 3) a lightweight pricing_hint/pricing_tier field to help routing decisions.

What changed (high level):
- API: GET /v1/models supports new query params: filter_profile (string), include_compat (boolean), pricing_hint (string) and streaming_safe (boolean) to annotate model capabilities for streaming callers. Responses include model.metadata.compatibility_preview (enum: none|openai|openai_partial), model.metadata.filter_profiles (list), and model.metadata.pricing_tier (string).
- Backend: catalog indexer updated to compute and persist filter profiles based on model performance metadata (latency P50/P95, kv-cache-friendly indicator, memory footprint). Added a lightweight compatibility-check pipeline that runs smoke checks for OpenAI function-calling semantics and sets the compatibility_preview flag.
- Server: model-list handler uses scoped profile templates to expand into query predicates; added caching for profile-expanded queries to avoid repeated index scans.
- Docs & SDKs: added examples and typing updates in Python/TS SDKs (backwards compatible: old fields untouched).

Compatibility notes: default behavior preserves the existing model-list response when filter_profile is absent. compatibility_preview defaults to 'none' until the smoke-check pipeline has run for a model. Pricing hints are advisory (routing may still consult explicit price tables).

Testing: unit tests for profile expansion, compatibility flagging, and JSON schema changes; integration test that validates streaming_safe semantics with the streaming router.

Related: Linear ENG-6125 tracks follow-up work for exposing filter_profile UI in Console; PM-187 documents product requirements for pricing tiers.

Checklist:
- [x] API + schema changes implemented
- [x] Indexer and pipeline to compute fields
- [x] SDK surface annotations updated (Python/TS)
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Migration notes and release notes prepared

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the compatibility_preview state machine (we keep an explicit 'pending' transitional window in the pipeline) and the cache TTL chosen for profile-expanded queries (30s by default).

This is backwards compatible; clients that do not opt in will see unchanged payloads. Admins: run the new compatibility_check pipeline to populate compatibility_preview flags before relying on them.

notes: Operational: after deploy, trigger catalog-compatibility-runner for historical models (can be throttled). Console team will consume filter_profiles for the UI; follow-up (ENG-6182) will add server-side ranking tweaks.
migration_steps: 1) Deploy API + indexer changes (backwards-compatible). 2) Run compatibility pipeline to populate compatibility_preview for models. 3) Optionally set default filter_profile in Console once signal looks good.
risk_assessment: Medium: adds new pipeline and query cache but maintains backwards compatibility. Primary risk is temporary inconsistency of compatibility_preview during initial runs. Mitigated via 'pending' state and conservative defaults.
security_considerations: No PII surface changes. Compatibility smoke checks run on local model artifacts only. Pricing hints are advisory and do not expose internal pricing tables.
testing_summary: Unit coverage + integration test that simulates streaming_safe routing and OpenAI function-call shim. Added a benchmark smoke job to ensure profile expansion cache doesn't regress p95 latency beyond 3%.
